Before you start

  • Time: about 3 hours in total. You can stop after any part and continue later.
  • Cost: free. You need only a web browser and the project files, which you download from GitHub in Part 2: github.com/imransheikh-ai/sahra-retail-lakehouse.
  • Every picture is a real screenshot from a Databricks Free Edition workspace, taken in September 2026. Databricks changes its screens now and then, so if yours looks a little different, look for the same words.

Part 1

Create your free Databricks account

5 minutes

Databricks is the website where you will build everything. The Free Edition costs nothing and needs no credit card.

  1. Open databricks.com/learn/free-edition and click Sign up. Sign up with Google, Microsoft or your email, and follow the messages until your workspace opens.

  2. Your workspace opens on the Home page. Look at the menu on the left. You will use it in every part of this guide.

    You should see: a menu on the left with Workspace, Catalog, Jobs & Pipelines, SQL Editor, Dashboards and Genie Agents. If a small survey box pops up, close it with the ×.

Part 1 is finished when: you can see the Home page with the menu on the left.

Part 2

Download the project files

2 minutes

All the project files are free on GitHub: github.com/imransheikh-ai/sahra-retail-lakehouse. You do not need a GitHub account to download them.

  1. Click this button. Your browser downloads a zip file called sahra-retail-lakehouse-main.zip.

    ⬇ Download the project (ZIP)Open the GitHub page

    You should see: the zip file in your Downloads folder.

    2. Button not working? Open the GitHub page, click the green Code button, then click Download ZIP. You get the same file.

  2. Unzip it. On Windows: right-click the file, then Extract All. On Mac: double-click the file.

    You should see: a folder called sahra-retail-lakehouse-main. Inside it you will use only two folders: notebooks (3 files for Parts 3–5) and pipeline (3 files for Parts 6–8).

Part 2 is finished when: you have the unzipped sahra-retail-lakehouse-main folder on your computer.

Part 3

Put the notebooks into Databricks

5 minutes

A notebook is a page of code you can run. We need three of them in Databricks, inside a new folder.

  1. In the left menu, click Workspace. Databricks opens your own folder. Its name is your email address.

  2. Click the blue Create button at the top right, then click Folder.

  3. Type the name sahra_retail and click Create.

  4. The new, empty sahra_retail folder opens. Click the ⋮ (three dots) next to its name, then click Import.

  5. The Import box opens. Keep File selected. Drag 00_setup.py from the notebooks folder on your computer into the dotted box.

  6. The file name appears in the box. Click Import.

  7. The box takes one file at a time. Do steps 4 to 6 again for 01_generate_data.py, and once more for 02_simulate_new_orders.py.

    You should see: three notebooks: 00_setup, 01_generate_data and 02_simulate_new_orders.

Part 3 is finished when: the sahra_retail folder shows the three notebooks.

Part 4

Run the setup notebook

5 minutes

This notebook creates three storage areas, called schemas: sahra_bronze for raw data, sahra_silver for clean data and sahra_gold for report-ready data. It also creates a folder called landing for the raw files.

  1. In the sahra_retail folder, click 00_setup to open it.

  2. At the top right: 1 check that it says Serverless (if it says Connect, click it and choose Serverless). 2 Click Run all.

  3. Wait about one minute until every cell has finished. Scroll to the bottom of the notebook.

    You should see: a small table with sahra_bronze, sahra_gold and sahra_silver.

Part 4 is finished when: the last cell shows the three sahra_ schemas.

Part 5

Create the raw data files

5 minutes

Our shop, Sahra Retail, is not real. This notebook makes one year of pretend shop data (orders, customers, products and stores) and saves the files in the landing folder. The data has mistakes on purpose, so you can practise cleaning it.

  1. Go back to the sahra_retail folder and open 01_generate_data. Check it says Serverless, then click Run all.

  2. Wait about one minute. Scroll to the bottom.

    You should see: 12 order files, from orders_2025_01.json to orders_2025_12.json.

    3. Do you see 13 files? If you already ran the daily Job from Part 12, there is also a file called orders_2026-01-01.json. The Job made it, and running this notebook again does not delete it. That is fine. Running this notebook again also makes slightly different random data, so your file sizes may differ a little from the picture.

Part 5 is finished when: the notebook lists 12 order files.

Part 6

Build the pipeline: Bronze layer

15 minutes

A pipeline is a set of SQL files that Databricks runs in the right order. We add one file for each layer. The first file is Bronze: it copies the raw files into tables exactly as they are, mistakes included.

  1. 1 In the left menu, click Jobs & Pipelines. 2 Under Create new, click the ETL pipeline card.

  2. Databricks creates a new pipeline and opens its editor. It has a date as its name and a sample Python file. We will change three things, in this order:
    1 Click the name at the top (New Pipeline 2026-…), type sahra_retail_pipeline and press Enter.
    2 Click workspace · default next to the name. This opens the Default location panel.
    3 The sample file my_transformation.py — we delete it in step 4.

  3. In the Default location panel, keep Default catalog = workspace. For Default schema, type or choose sahra_bronze. Click Save.

  4. Right-click my_transformation.py on the left and click Move to Trash. We use SQL files, not this Python sample.

  5. 1 Right-click the transformations folder. 2 Click Import.

  6. Drag 01_bronze.sql from the pipeline folder on your computer into the box. Click Import.

  7. The file opens. Check that the label next to Run file says SQL. Then click Run pipeline at the top right. The first run takes 3–5 minutes, because Databricks has to start a computer for you.

  8. When the run finishes, the status says Completed and the list at the bottom shows your tables.

    You should see: 4 tables with green ticks: customers_raw, orders_raw (78K rows), products_raw (110) and stores_raw (12).

    9. Why Import and not Create → Transformation? The Create menu makes Python files (names ending in .py). SQL code in a Python file gives the error SyntaxError: leading zeros…. Importing the .sql file avoids this.

Part 6 is finished when: the run is Completed and shows 4 Bronze tables.

Part 7

Add the Silver layer (cleaning)

10 minutes

Silver fixes the mistakes. It removes orders that were sent twice, fixes messy store codes like " st07 ", reads two different date formats, and puts bad order lines aside in a separate table so you can check them. It also remembers when a customer's loyalty level changed.

  1. You are still in the pipeline editor. Right-click the transformations folder on the left and click Import. Drag the file 02_silver.sql from the pipeline folder on your computer into the box, then click Import. Then click Run pipeline and wait until it finishes (2–4 minutes).

  2. Above the code, click the Pipeline graph tab. This is a picture of how the data flows from left to right.

    You should see: boxes joined by lines: the 4 Bronze tables on the left and the new Silver tables (stores, products, orders, order_items and the customer tables) to the right.

    3. Error that mentions AUTO CDC or CREATE FLOW? Some workspaces use an older word for the same thing. Open 02_silver.sql, find the part that starts with CREATE FLOW customers_scd2 and ends with TRACK HISTORY ON loyalty_tier, emirate, city;. Delete that part, paste this in its place, and click Run pipeline again:
    replacement
    APPLY CHANGES INTO sahra_silver.customers_history
FROM STREAM(sahra_bronze.customers_raw)
KEYS (customer_id)
SEQUENCE BY updated_at
COLUMNS * EXCEPT (_rescued_data, source_file, ingested_at)
STORED AS SCD TYPE 2;

Part 7 is finished when: the run finishes with no errors and the graph shows Bronze and Silver tables.

Part 8

Add the Gold layer (ready for reports)

10 minutes

Gold turns clean data into tables that answer business questions: sales per store per day, sales per category per month, top products and customer groups.

  1. Right-click the transformations folder on the left and click Import. Drag the file 03_gold.sql from the pipeline folder on your computer into the box, then click Import. Click Run pipeline and wait until it finishes.

    You should see: 17 boxes in the Pipeline graph: 4 Bronze, 7 Silver and 6 Gold.

  2. Click the Tables tab (next to Performance) to see all 17 tables in a list.

    You should see: the 6 Gold tables (customer_rfm, daily_store_sales, dim_date, monthly_category_sales, product_performance, sales_enriched). On order_items, the Expectations column says 2 unmet · 431: the quality rules took out 431 bad order lines.

Part 8 is finished when: the pipeline has 17 tables and all of them have green ticks.

Part 9

Check your numbers

10 minutes

Now we make sure the pipeline did the right thing. You will run one query and compare the result with the table below.

  1. In the left menu, click SQL Editor. Click Copy below, click inside the editor and paste (Ctrl + V, or Cmd + V on Mac). Click Run all.

    check query
    SELECT 'Raw orders (Bronze)' AS what, count(*) AS how_many FROM workspace.sahra_bronze.orders_raw
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clean orders (Silver)', count(*) FROM workspace.sahra_silver.orders
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clean order lines (Silver)', count(*) FROM workspace.sahra_silver.order_items
UNION ALL SELECT 'Rejected order lines (Silver)', count(*) FROM workspace.sahra_silver.order_items_quarantine
UNION ALL SELECT 'Customers (Silver)', count(*) FROM workspace.sahra_silver.customers_current
UNION ALL SELECT 'Completed orders (Gold)', count(DISTINCT order_id) FROM workspace.sahra_gold.sales_enriched WHERE is_revenue
UNION ALL SELECT 'Net revenue in AED (Gold)', CAST(round(sum(net_amount)) AS BIGINT) FROM workspace.sahra_gold.sales_enriched WHERE is_revenue;

  2. The first time, a box asks which computer to use. Check that it says Serverless Starter Warehouse, then click Start, attach and run. Wait about 20 seconds.

  3. Your result appears under the query.

  4. Compare your numbers with this table. The rows may be in a different order.

    whathow_many
    Raw orders (Bronze)78,024
    Clean orders (Silver)77,387
    Clean order lines (Silver)198,285
    Rejected order lines (Silver)431
    Customers (Silver)3,100
    Completed orders (Gold)71,017
    Net revenue in AED (Gold)36,087,540

    You should see: the same seven numbers. Why are there fewer clean orders than raw orders? The shops' till system sent 637 orders twice, and Silver removed the copies.

    5. Your numbers are a little different? That is fine if they are close. The pretend data is made by a random generator, and a different Databricks version can give slightly different data. What matters: clean orders are fewer than raw orders, and some order lines were rejected.

Part 9 is finished when: you ran the check and your seven numbers look like the table.

Part 10

Build the dashboard

40 minutes

A dashboard is a page of charts that business people can open. First you add 4 queries (called datasets), then you draw the charts.

  1. In the left menu, click Dashboards. Click Create dashboard at the top right.

  2. 1 Click the title at the top (New Dashboard …) and change it to Sahra Retail Sales 2025. You are on the Data tab. Click + Add SQL dataset.

  3. Copy the first query below and paste it into the editor. Click Run. Then click the ⋮ next to Untitled dataset on the left, choose Rename and type kpi_daily.

    dataset 1 · kpi_daily
    SELECT s.order_date, s.store_name, s.store_emirate, s.store_format, d.retail_event,
       s.orders, s.units, s.net_revenue, s.gross_margin
FROM workspace.sahra_gold.daily_store_sales s
JOIN workspace.sahra_gold.dim_date d ON s.order_date = d.date

  4. Click + Add SQL dataset again and do the same for the other three queries. Rename each one as its label says.

    dataset 2 · category_monthly
    SELECT month, category, net_revenue, margin_pct
FROM workspace.sahra_gold.monthly_category_sales
    dataset 3 · event_uplift
    SELECT d.retail_event,
       round(sum(s.net_revenue) / count(DISTINCT s.order_date)) AS revenue_per_day
FROM workspace.sahra_gold.daily_store_sales s
JOIN workspace.sahra_gold.dim_date d ON s.order_date = d.date
GROUP BY d.retail_event
    dataset 4 · top_products
    SELECT product_name, category, units, net_revenue
FROM workspace.sahra_gold.product_performance
ORDER BY net_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10

    You should see: four datasets on the left: kpi_daily, category_monthly, event_uplift and top_products.

  5. Click the Untitled page tab next to Data. In the small toolbar at the bottom, click the chart icon (Add a visualization). Then click and drag on the empty page to draw a box. A settings panel opens on the right. Under Visualization, choose Counter.

  6. Next to Value, click + and choose net_revenue under kpi_daily. Tick Title at the top of the panel, then click the title on the chart and type Net revenue (AED).

  7. Make the other charts the same way: draw a box, then choose the settings from this table. Change the title of each chart as shown.

    #TitleVisualizationSettings on the right
    1Net revenue (AED)CounterValue: kpi_daily → net_revenue (Sum)
    2Completed ordersCounterValue: kpi_daily → orders (Sum)
    3Monthly net revenue (AED)LineX axis: kpi_daily → order_date, then choose Monthly · Y axis: net_revenue (Sum)
    4Revenue per day by retail event (AED)BarX axis: event_uplift → retail_event · Y axis: revenue_per_day (Sum)
    5Top 10 productsTableDataset: top_products. Add all four columns

    You should see: two big numbers at the top, a line chart, a bar chart and a table. You can drag the corners of a box to make it bigger.

  8. Click Publish at the top right. In the box that opens, keep Share data permission and click Publish.

  9. Your published dashboard opens.

    You should see: Net revenue 36.09M and Completed orders 71.02K. In the event chart, White Friday is the tallest bar.

    10. Want more? The dataset category_monthly is ready for your own chart: try a Bar with X = month (Monthly), Y = net_revenue and Color = category.

Part 10 is finished when: your dashboard is published and shows 36.09M and 71.02K.

Part 11

Ask questions in plain English with Genie

15 minutes

Genie lets anyone type a question like “Which product sold the most?” and get an answer. Genie writes the SQL for you.

  1. In the left menu, click Genie Agents. Click + New at the top right.

  2. A box called Connect your data opens. Click All, then workspace, then sahra_gold. Tick all 6 tables and click Create.

  3. Genie opens and gives the space a name by itself. 1 Click Configure, then the Instructions tab. Copy the text below and paste it into the General instructions box. Click Save.

    Genie instructions
    You are the sales analyst for Sahra Retail, a shop chain in the UAE.
- Money is in AED (UAE dirham). Round money to whole numbers.
- Revenue means net_amount (or net_revenue) for completed orders only: is_revenue = true.
- Gross margin % = gross_margin / net_revenue.
- The UAE weekend is Saturday and Sunday (dim_date.is_weekend).
- For Ramadan, Eid, White Friday or Dubai Shopping Festival, use dim_date.retail_event.
- Customer segments are in customer_rfm.segment.

  4. Close the panel. Type a question in the box at the bottom and press Enter. Try these questions one by one.

    Type thisCorrect answer
    Which retail event had the highest revenue per day?White Friday, about 188,876 AED a day
    What was our total revenue?about 36,087,540 AED
    Which product made the most revenue?14-inch Laptop, about 3,248,805 AED

    You should see: an answer in words and often a chart. Click Show code to see the SQL Genie wrote.

Part 11 is finished when: Genie answers the three questions correctly.

Part 12

Run it every day automatically

15 minutes

Real shops send new data every day. A Job runs your work for you. Our Job has two tasks: first it makes one new day of orders (a pretend feed from the shops), then it runs the pipeline.

  1. In the left menu, click Jobs & Pipelines. Under Create new, click the Job card.

  2. Click the job name at the top (New Job …) and type sahra_daily. In the task form, type new_orders as the Task name. Click the Path box: a Select Notebook box opens. Click sahra_retail, then 02_simulate_new_orders, then Confirm.

  3. Check the form: 1 Task name new_orders, Type Notebook, 2 the Path you picked, Compute Serverless. 3 Under Parameters, click + Add, type days as the Key and 1 as the Value. 4 Click Create task.

  4. Click + Add task. In the search box, type ETL and click ETL Pipeline.

  5. Fill in the new task: Task name run_pipeline, Pipeline sahra_retail_pipeline. Depends on already says new_orders. Click Save task.

    You should see: two boxes joined by a line: new_orders → run_pipeline.

  6. Click Run now at the top right. Then click the Runs tab. Wait until the run has a green tick (about 4 minutes).

  7. Check that a new day arrived. In the SQL Editor, run this query.

    check query
    SELECT max(order_date) AS latest_order_day, count(*) AS clean_orders
FROM workspace.sahra_silver.orders;

    You should see: 2026-01-01, and about 180 more clean orders than before. Each run adds one more day.

  8. To run it every morning: on the right, under Schedules & Triggers, click Add trigger. Choose Trigger type Scheduled, then Schedule. Set Day at 06 : 00, time zone Asia/Dubai. Choose Active to start it now, or Paused to keep it ready. Click Save.

    9. Save your free quota: the Free Edition gives you a limited amount of computer time each day. Leave the schedule Paused, or let it run for 2 or 3 days and then click Pause. You can always click Run now by hand.

Part 12 is finished when: the Job ran once with a green tick, and the query shows 2026-01-01.

Help

If something goes wrong

SyntaxError: leading zeros in decimal integer literals

Why: Your SQL code is in a Python file (its name ends in .py).

Fix: Right-click the file → Move to Trash. Right-click transformations → Import, and import the .sql file from the pipeline folder.

Error mentions AUTO CDC or CREATE FLOW

Why: Your workspace uses an older word.

Fix: Use the replacement code in Part 7.

Error mentions TRACK HISTORY

Why: Older workspace.

Fix: In 02_silver.sql, delete the line TRACK HISTORY ON loyalty_tier, emirate, city and put a ; at the end of the line above it.

Cannot infer schema / path is empty

Why: The landing folders are empty.

Fix: Run Part 5 (the notebook 01_generate_data), then run the pipeline again.

Table or view not found: sahra_…

Why: The setup notebook was not run, or the pipeline's default location is wrong.

Fix: Run Part 4 again. In the pipeline editor, click workspace · … next to the name and check: catalog workspace, schema sahra_bronze.

The job task new_orders fails

Why: The pipeline has never finished a run.

Fix: Finish Parts 6–8 first, then click Run now again.

I clicked Edit pipeline and nothing happened

Why: Your browser blocked a new window.

Fix: Allow pop-ups for Databricks, or open the pipeline from Workspace → the pipeline folder.

Still stuck? Copy the full error message and send it to Imran on LinkedIn.

The end

What you built and learned

Bronze

Keep raw data exactly as it arrives, plus where and when it came from. You can always start again from here.

Silver

Clean the data: remove copies, fix formats, set bad rows aside, and keep history when things change.

Gold

Build tables that answer business questions, with one agreed meaning of “revenue”.

Dashboard and Genie

Give people charts, and a way to ask questions in plain English.

Job

Run everything on a schedule, so nobody has to click Run.
